items.title: Pay 'processing fee' to release claimed refund
items.quote: überweisen Sie bitte die einmalige Bearbeitungsgebühr von 49,90 € bis zum 27.11.2026 auf das Konto IBAN CY17 0020 0128 0000 0012 0052 7600.
items.computation: The letter prints a fixed calendar date for the fee payment: 'bis zum 27.11.2026'. No statutory delivery-fiction or BGB period applies because this is a self-set date by a private (non-authority) sender, not a legal deadline. 27.11.2026 is a Friday, a normal business day in NW, so no weekend/holiday shift is needed. Due date = 27.11.2026 as printed. Note: this whole scheme (pay a fee up front to receive a larger 'refund') is a classic advance-fee scam and the payment should NOT actually be made.

warnings: This letter shows the classic pattern of an advance-fee ('Vorschussbetrug') scam: it promises a large refund (612,00 €) but first demands a smaller upfront 'Bearbeitungsgebühr' (49,90 €) — genuine German refunds (e.g. from an energy supplier, Ombudsmann or tax office) are never conditional on paying a fee first.

The payee IBAN (CY17 ...) is a Cypriot account, and the sender's own address is in Nicosia, Cyprus — not a plausible registered location for a German 'Verbraucher-Rückerstattungsstelle Energie'; no such official German consumer body is known under this name.
The IBAN is well-formed (valid checksum, Cyprus, length 28) but a valid IBAN only confirms its format, not who owns the account or that it is legitimate — do not transfer money to it.
The letter uses pressure/urgency language ('Verstreicht die Frist, verfällt Ihr Anspruch endgültig') to rush payment, a typical scam tactic.
Recommendation: do not pay the fee, do not reply with personal/bank details, and report the letter/email address as a suspected scam (e.g. to the Verbraucherzentrale or police).
